 WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (CBS12) — The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has lifted a ground stop for flights headed to President Donald J. Trump International Airport in West Palm Beach on Wednesday afternoon, following earlier flight delays caused by thunderstorms.
 According to the FAA, the ground stop began at 1:51 p.m. and was in effect until 3:15 p.m. due to airport volume.
 CBS12 News' Antoinette DelBel is at DJT airport and reports that there are no more delays as of 4:10 p.m.
 The restriction applied to flights departing from three FAA air traffic control regions: Atlanta, Jacksonville and Miami.
 See also: Florida stepfather stops alleged sexual assault of 15-year-old girl walking dog 
 These regions cover multiple airports, meaning flights headed to West Palm Beach from several locations could be affected.
 Earlier Wednesday, the FAA reported that flights departing from Trump International Airport were experiencing average delays of 15 minutes and increasing because of thunderstorms.
 Travelers are encouraged to check with their airlines for the latest flight information before heading to the airport.
